core.text: Propose moving the source-to-rack feeding function from powered trolley to the existing hand carrier, paced by clock boundaries. Start B4 at boundary 2; start B5 through B12 at boundaries 3 through 10 respectively. Each arrives one minute later. Start inspection at 0 and immediately whenever its next carrier is eligible. This adds a concrete boundary dispatch schedule to consecutive hand carrying; it is a proposal, not an observed run.

Closest rival: trolley B4-B7 from 0 to 3, trolley B8-B11 from 3 to 6, then hand carry B12 from 6 to 7. Provisional model predictions are twelve correct releases at 13 for both schedules, nine transfer minutes for migration versus seven for rival. Migration therefore has no predicted labor-ranking advantage among complete successes.

Replay each schedule through the finite boundary ledger. Record carrier identities unloaded, completed correct seals and bracket counts, separate clerk occupied intervals, rack occupancy, waits and charge use. Check B9 correction from 8 to 10 and final release at 13; packing marks cannot establish success. The comparison separates timely feeding from transport-count rhetoric.

residue.text: Proposed burden ledger: transfer clerk performs nine nonoverlapping manual trips; inspection clerk performs thirteen busy minutes, uses the spare bracket and twelve seals. Migration predicts no unloading waits, rack peak three, and zero trolley allowances consumed. Clock/ledger maintenance adds zero modeled labor. Removing charge dependence does not remove manual labor, the rack or the counting-surface dependency.

Leave the fresh attacker to challenge the new timed manual-feed dependency. Candidate defeat observations: any inspection idle minute, an unloading wait, fewer than twelve correct releases at 13, or an occupied-minute ranking loss against a successful rival. Starvation/blocking predictions remain unverified hypotheses; no final attack is selected.

B9 discrepancy cause, later request adaptation, empirical performance and global optimality remain unknown. No extra failures or arrivals may be assumed. Boundary calculations predict this stipulated window only; they establish no future maintenance or replenishment behavior.

tension.account_a: Clock-paced hand feeding keeps inspection continuously supplied through the existing rack.
tension.account_b: Attack hypothesis: the proposed dispatch timing creates starvation or blocked unloading within the stated boundary rules.
tension.prediction_a: Nine source carriers arrive by 11, no transfer waits occur, inspection stays busy, and twelve correct releases finish at 13.
tension.prediction_b: The same boundary replay exposes an inspection idle interval or unloading wait, producing fewer than twelve correct releases at 13 or more than nine transfer busy minutes.
